title: Two Active Sentora instances declare a Maximum Exposure of 0 USD while their on-chain deposit limits permit 50 million
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.7.5.2.5.1 and A...7.6.2.5.1 each state, under Off-chain Operational Parameters: "The Maximum Exposure for this Instance is **0 USD**."

Both instances are listed Active, both publish inflow and outflow `RateLimitID`s (A...7.5.2.3, A...7.6.2.3), and both set deposit limits of `maxAmount` 50,000,000 with a 50,000,000-per-day slope — 50 million PYUSD for one, 50 million RLUSD for the other (A...7.5.2.4.1, A...7.6.2.4.1). Each also has a `maxExchangeRate` configured (A...7.5.4.1, A...7.6.4.1), which is the protection required *for deposits*.

So the on-chain state is fully provisioned to allow 50 million of exposure, and a sentence says the permitted exposure is zero. Nothing in the rate-limit contract consults that sentence.

The most plausible reading is staged onboarding: the instance is approved, its keys are registered and its protections are set, but capital allocation is deliberately withheld pending something — a risk model, a counterparty milestone, a governance step. Under that reading the configuration is correct and the zero is a live policy instruction.

But the mechanism to express it already exists and was not used. Setting `maxAmount` to zero would make the intent self-enforcing, because `triggerRateLimitDecrease` reverts on `zero-maxAmount` (A...1.3.4) — the same technique the Artifact mandates for the untested LayerZero function (A...2.1.2.13.1.2). Choosing prose over the kill switch for a zero-exposure instruction leaves a 50 million gap between what governance intends and what a relayer can do, and it is the second instance of this pattern after the ACRDX cap in A...3.1.1.3.2.5.1.
description: The Sentora PYUSD and RLUSD Morpho Vault V2 instances pair a prose ceiling of zero with enforced 50,000,000 per day deposit budgets — the policy gate is not the one the contract checks.
